title: NonStationaryBrachistochrone: reproducibility package for controlled-rail brachistochrones in non-stationary spacetimes
description:
NonStationaryBrachistochrone provides symbolic derivations, numerical verification scripts, figure generators and manuscript sources for controlled-rail brachistochrones in non-stationary spacetimes. It supports the companion studies of FLRW and Vaidya geometries (Paper I) and conformal Kerr, or Thakurta–Kerr, spacetimes (Paper II).

This release makes the whole repository readable in English and the verification results machine-readable. The scientific results are unchanged.

  • English names and text throughout. Scripts and figures with Italian names have been renamed, including the three cited in the manuscripts (bvp_fixed_endpoints.py, deltaphi_full_pipeline.py, make_figures_vaidya.py). Comments, printed messages, figure labels and the per-geometry result notes are in English. The README maps the old names, cited by earlier releases and by the submitted manuscripts, to the new ones.
  • Superseded scripts set apart. Exploratory and superseded scripts have been moved to NonStationaryMetrics/exploratory/, whose README states what each one did and what replaced it. No cited result depends on them. Scripts that had no entry in the documentation are now described.
  • Versioned JSON results. The regression runner and the Sage checking runner read the checked quantities from versioned JSON files with a strict schema, instead of parsing printed messages. Tests check the JSON contracts and compare the JSON values with the printed logs.
  • Single copies. Duplicated genus-two Sage scripts have been removed; each exists once, in KerrScripts/.
  • Symbolic proof of the umbilicity minors. A Mathematica script now proves, for general parameters, the order-a² minors of inclined central planes of the optical data (Paper II, appendix E), previously checked at sampled points.
  • Consistent metadata. Paper I prints the current checksum of its validation script, and the manuscripts in the repository cite this release.

Verification used a clean copy of the release with a fresh Python 3.13 environment installed from requirements-lock.txt. The 12 regression checks passed both from the JSON results and from the printed messages. For the 12 regression programs, the numerical values in the human-readable output match v1.8.3 at the printed precision when run in the same environment; the JSON results retain the values before display rounding. The six Sage checks, the JSON contract, consistency and parser tests, the Paper I build tests and the provenance verification passed. The Paper I build regenerated all 13 required figures and produced a 67-page manuscript; Paper II compiled to 134 pages.

Generated figures, compiled PDFs and raw datasets are regenerated using the documented commands. Verification maps distinguish symbolic identities, numerical checks, sampled evidence and archived certificates. Manuscripts submitted before this release cite earlier releases, which remain archived under their own version DOIs; the README maps their script names to the current ones.
